evidence.claim: The upstream hook-dispatch-v1.sh is 128 lines of bash; its bulk is argument parsing, harness validation and a path-safety guard, which in Node are a destructure, a set test and path.relative.
No dependency evaluated: a hook with a 1 s budget must import nothing heavy, and the project ships zero runtime dependencies.

candidates.name: Static import map from hook id to payload module

evidence.claim: A static map lets the manifest-resolution test assert that every id in hooks.json has a handler WITHOUT executing it; a dynamic import path cannot express that statically.
Cost: every payload module is loaded on every hook invocation. Measured headroom is large (48 ms floor against 1000 ms), but this is the trade the next candidate weighs.

Parsing hooks.json: all 31 hooks pass `--hook <id>` in args (31 distinct ids), while the matcher-level `id` field is present on only 4 of 14 matcher entries. The two spellings also differ (`sessionstart:kbd-control` vs `sessionstart-kbd-control`).

candidates.decision_rationale: Keys on the `--hook` argument, never the matcher-level `id`: keying on `id` would cover 4 hooks and silently miss 27.

candidates.name: Lazy await import() per hook id

evidence.claim: Loads only the needed payload, so marginally faster, but defeats cand-102s static assertion and makes a missing module a RUNTIME error on the hook path — the exact failure mode (MODULE_NOT_FOUND before any of our code runs) this phase exists to prevent.

candidates.name: node:perf_hooks + spawnSync round-trips for cold-start measurement

evidence.claim: process.hrtime.bigint and performance.now are both present in Node 22+; node:test has no bench API in this version, checked directly.
Measured on this host with 10 spawnSync round-trips per case: bare node -e 46 ms, empty .mjs 48 ms, .mjs importing three lib/platform modules 59 ms (medians).
npm view: tinybench@6.2.0, MIT, zero dependencies, modified 2026-09-09 — healthy and well maintained.
Rejected on fit, not health: it measures in-process function throughput. The quantity that matters here is PROCESS start, which only spawn round-trips capture.
npm view: mitata@1.0.34, MIT, zero dependencies, modified 2025-02-04. Same fit problem as cand-105, and a year older.
Hooks receive a JSON payload on stdin; node:fs readFileSync(0) reads fd 0 synchronously with no dependency, which suits a synchronous 1 s hook.
Not covered: it must tolerate EMPTY stdin — the orchestrator action path passes none — and must not block when stdin is a TTY. Both are test cases, not assumptions.

candidates.name: Manifest-resolution test derived from hooks.json

evidence.claim: The source pack shipped a plugin payload whose hooks.json referenced scripts/hook-entry.mjs without packaging it; every hook event then failed in Node loader with MODULE_NOT_FOUND before any of its code ran. Fixed upstream at fcccc9d by deriving the packaged file list FROM hooks.json.
The rule is already written in rules/src/project/node-scripts.md; this candidate is the test that enforces it here.

Parsing hooks.json: all 31 hooks pass `--hook <id>` in args (31 distinct ids), while the matcher-level `id` field is present on only 4 of 14 matcher entries. The two spellings also differ (`sessionstart:kbd-control` vs `sessionstart-kbd-control`).

candidates.decision_rationale: Derives its id list from every `--hook` argument in hooks.json, not from matcher-level `id` and not from a hand-kept list — the hand-kept list is what shipped a payload with no entry file.

build_required.need: harness exec-form support probe — Does this harness accept exec form (command + args) in a project hooks.json, or only a shell-string command?
build_required.why_no_candidate: Not a library gap: it is a property of the harness that no package can supply or settle. The source pack plugin hooks.json uses exec form for all 31 entries. Live user settings on this machine use {"type":"command","command":"<shell string>"} with no args: 6 entries inspected across ~/.claude/settings.json, settings.local.json and .claude/settings.json, 0 using args. Different surfaces, so this is neither confirmation nor refutation. If exec form is unsupported, a shell string puts sh -c / PowerShell back in the hook path, which C1 and C3 forbid. The design would have to change before any payload is written. Resolution: Plan task 1 after the goal-1 re-review: register one trivial exec-form hook and observe whether it fires. Empirical, cheap, and blocking.
